title: automation: tenant-scoped RBAC bundles and bootstrap permissions for Private installer
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Private deployments require tenant-isolated RBAC and a safe bootstrap flow for first-run operators. This PR automates generation and application of RBAC policy bundles for the Private installer so tenants are provisioned with least-privilege roles, and the installer can perform an idempotent bootstrap without leaving broad cluster-wide permissions.

Summary of changes:
- Add tenant-scoped role templates and policy bundle generator (helm chart + terraform outputs)
- Introduce a bootstrap ServiceAccount and controller role with constrained permissions for initial registration flows
- Add installer hook to apply per-tenant policies using the generated bundle (kubectl/apply compatible manifests)
- Enhance Helm chart for private-installer to accept rbac.bundle values and TTL-based rotation for bootstrap credentials
- Terraform module updates: new outputs for policy_bundle_url and bootstrap_sa_secret; optional apply_policy boolean for opt-in automation
- Idempotent upgrade path and rollback handling: policy application is guarded by a policy revision annotation and a safe re-apply strategy to avoid lateral privilege escalation

Why: Previously RBAC bundles were produced manually and applied by operators which led to misconfigurations and incident SUP-981. Automating generation + controlled bootstrap reduces human error and provides a reproducible, auditable process for tenant isolation.

review_comments: Leo Martinez (review): Can we avoid storing bootstrap SA secrets in plaintext in Terraform state? Suggested: output the secret name only and return the secret via API during install.
Author (Asha): Updated Terraform to only emit secret name and added a secure retrieval path in the installer. See terraform/modules/private-installer/outputs.tf change.
Sofia Huang (review): Please add an explicit e2e test that verifies tenant A cannot access tenant B resources after bundle apply.
Author: Added tests/integration/test_rbac_bundle_apply.sh and wired into CI. Also added a small policy-revision annotation check to prevent accidental downgrade.
Marco Alvarez (approval): Verified helm chart values and upgrade path. Integration tests passed in staging. Approving for squash-merge.
release_notes: Automated RBAC bundles for Private installer: tenant-scoped roles, bootstrap SA flow, helm + terraform integration. Operators can opt into automated policy application via chart/terraform flags. Includes migration guide to safely rotate bootstrap credentials.
upgrade_notes: When upgrading from <2026-01 versions, set terraform var 'apply_policy' to false for the first run to generate bundles offline and validate. To opt-in, flip 'apply_policy' to true and run a rollout; the installer will apply the policy only if the 'policy.redwood.com/revision' annotation differs. Bootstrap SA secret rotation is implemented with TTL; follow docs/private/rbac-automation.md for secret rotation steps.
testing_notes: Local repro: make dev-setup && scripts/bootstrap-local.sh --tenant test-tenant; run tests/integration/test_rbac_bundle_apply.sh. Staging: helm upgrade --install private-installer ./charts/private-installer -f ci/values-staging.yaml and run ci/integration-pipeline which includes tenant isolation smoke tests.
notes_for_ops:
- Terraform no longer stores bootstrap secrets in state; secret names are emitted instead.
- Ensure cluster operator has permissions to create RoleBindings in tenant namespaces for initial apply.
- Policy bundles are stored on the installer artifact bucket; object URLs are exported as terraform outputs for auditing.
- In air-gapped/on-prem installs, set 'rbac.bundle.localPath' to provide pre-generated bundle tarball.
